source.title: toSnakeCase() does not treat Unicode whitespace as separators

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Description

The `.toSnakeCase()` string expression extension only converts the plain ASCII
space (U+0020) and `-` into `_`. Other Unicode whitespace is either kept in the
output as an invisible character or deleted entirely, which silently corrupts
the generated identifier.

### Minimal reproduction

In the JS snippets below, `\u00A0` is a non-breaking space, `\t` a tab and
`\u2003` an em space. The actual expression inputs contain those characters,
not the escape sequences.

```js
'first\u00A0name'.toSnakeCase() // 'first\u00A0name', expected 'first_name'  (NBSP retained)
'first\tname'.toSnakeCase()     // 'first\tname',     expected 'first_name'  (tab retained)
'first\u2003name'.toSnakeCase() // 'firstname',       expected 'first_name'  (em space deleted, words glued)
'I am a test!'.toSnakeCase()    // 'i_am_a_test'      (plain ASCII space, works as expected)
```

The same calls as n8n expressions (the special whitespace is invisible in the
source; NBSP = U+00A0, TAB = U+0009, EMSP = U+2003):

```
={{ "first<NBSP>name".toSnakeCase() }}  // "first<NBSP>name", expected "first_name"
={{ "first<TAB>name".toSnakeCase() }}   // "first<TAB>name",  expected "first_name"
={{ "first<EMSP>name".toSnakeCase() }}  // "firstname",       expected "first_name"
={{ "I am a test!".toSnakeCase() }}     // "i_am_a_test"      (works as expected)
```

### Expected behavior

All Unicode whitespace separators should behave like a plain ASCII space and
produce `_`, i.e. `"first_name"`. Plain spaces, hyphens, lowercasing,
punctuation removal and existing underscores should keep working as before.

### Impact

The output of `.toSnakeCase()` is typically used as an object key, file name,
column name or field name. Invisible characters (NBSP, tab, newline, ideographic
space) survive into the key, so later lookups and comparisons fail; whitespace
in the U+2000-U+206F range is removed and two words are glued together. Both
cases produce silently wrong data in workflows that normalise incoming text.
Text copied from web pages, PDFs and spreadsheets frequently contains these
characters, so this is a common input path.

### Additional context

The implementation lives in
`packages/workflow/src/extensions/string-extensions.ts` and is mirrored in
`packages/@n8n/expression-runtime/src/extensions/string-extensions.ts` for the
isolated VM; both copies are affected.
